name: Roborock Local Server
use_label: Run a Roborock vacuum without the cloud
one_liner: Runs Roborock's cloud backend on your own network so the vacuum keeps maps and controls without internet.

text.why: Roborock vacuums store maps locally but route map data through Roborock's cloud, and keep restarting their network when they can't reach it — so cutting them off the internet broke them.
text.take: It cuts the cloud dependency in software alone, without opening the device.
build: It runs HTTPS and MQTT on your LAN and redirects DNS so the vacuum connects to it instead of Roborock. No disassembly, soldering or bootloader unlocking, and new vacuums work without prior cloud registration. Install with Docker Compose or as a Home Assistant add-on.

who.role: Home Assistant users who want their Roborock vacuum off the internet.

start.text: Check the network requirements in the install guide, run the server with Docker Compose or the Home Assistant add-on, then run onboarding from a second machine.

caveat: You need to manage your home network yourself (DNS changes, certificates). The README notes upstream authentication changes are the most frequent point of failure.
